message.reasoning:
We need to imagine three experts each proposing test cases stepwise and then finally provide complete JUnit test file. The answer should present the process? The instruction: "All experts will propose one test cases for each method, share it with the group, and then proceed to the next step. If any expert realizes they're wrong at any point, they leave. ... At the end they must propose one complete ... test file." So we need to simulate that discussion and then give final test file. Provide narrative of experts and their proposals, then final test class. Ensure test file includes comprehensive tests for each method: tokenType, reset static, Doctype getters/setters, Tag methods (newAttribute, finaliseTag, name, normalName, etc.), StartTag toString, EndTag toString, Comment, Character, EOF, the isX/asX methods.

We need JUnit 4 imports, use assertEquals, assertTrue, assertFalse, etc. Use reflection to access protected members? Some methods are package-private default (no modifier) and final in same package. The test class should be in same package org.jsoup.parser to access package-private classes. So include package org.jsoup.parser; at top.

Create tests covering:

- Token tokenType string matches class name.

- static reset on StringBuilder.

- Doctype reset clears fields.

- Doctype getters after modification.

- Tag reset clears fields.

- Tag name(), normalName(), name(String), isSelfClosing.

- Tag newAttribute handling attribute name trimming, empty value, null value.

- Tag finaliseTag triggers newAttribute when pending attribute.

- Tag appendTagName and attribute functions.

- StartTag toString with/without attributes.

- EndTag toString.

- Comment getData and toString.

- Character data and toString.

- EOF reset returns same.

- isDoctype etc.

Edge cases: attribute name only whitespace -> trimmed empty -> not added. Empty attribute value via setEmptyAttributeValue.

Also test ensureAttributeValue conversion from pendingAttributeValueS to builder when second call.

We'll need to instantiate Tag via StartTag or EndTag (since Tag is abstract). Use StartTag for attribute tests.

Test pending attribute value building: call appendAttributeValue("a"), then appendAttributeValue("b") and ensure value "ab". Also test pendingAttributeValueS path: first call set value via appendAttributeValue("x") (pendingAttributeValue length zero -> pendingAttributeValueS = "x"), then second call appendAttributeValue("y") should move pendingAttributeValueS to builder and then append "y". Ensure attribute value becomes "xy".

Also test attribute with no value (hasEmptyAttributeValue false, hasPendingAttributeValue false) leads to null value.

Test attribute with empty value: setEmptyAttributeValue then newAttribute leads to attribute with "".

Testing newAttribute with whitespace name: set pendingAttributeName = "  " (via appendAttributeName maybe) and newAttribute should not add.

We'll need to access pendingAttributeName etc. Those are private. Can't directly set. Use the public methods: appendAttributeName, setEmptyAttributeValue, etc. So to test newAttribute with whitespace name, we can call appendAttributeName("  "), then newAttribute. Should trim to empty and not add attribute.

Test attributes after newAttribute: attributes map contains correct.

Also test finaliseTag when pending attribute exists.

Test StartTag nameAttr method sets tagName and attributes.

Test toString for StartTag with attributes: attributes toString returns something like "key=val". Use Attributes from jsoup; we can create new Attributes and put entries.

But Attributes class is part of Jsoup library; we assume present. Use new Attributes().put("href","http://example.com").

Now produce final test file.

Will start with ###Test START## then code then ###Test END##.

Let's craft.
